steps.title: Where to find the settings
steps.body: Find the gear icon ⚙️ on your home screen — this is the icon for Settings. This is where you control almost everything on your phone.

steps.title: Checking storage space
steps.body: Go to Settings > Storage to see how much space is left. Is your phone almost full? It often runs slower. Remove old photos or apps you no longer use.

steps.title: Saving battery
steps.body: Under Settings > Battery you can see which apps use the most battery. Turn on 'Battery saver' if your phone runs out of charge quickly.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Go to your own phone's settings and check how much storage space is left.

steps.title: Opening the app store
steps.body: On Android this is the Play Store, on iPhone the App Store. Search for an app by name, check the reviews, and tap 'Install'.

steps.title: Removing an app
steps.body: Press and hold the app icon on your home screen until a menu appears, and choose 'Uninstall' or 'Remove app'. Your data within the app usually disappears too.

steps.title: Keeping apps up to date
steps.body: Apps regularly receive updates, often to close security gaps. Turn on automatic updates in your app store's settings, so you don't have to remember this yourself.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Search the app store for an app you're interested in, without installing it.

steps.title: What is a voice assistant?
steps.body: A voice assistant (Siri on iPhone, Google Assistant on Android) listens to your voice and carries out a command, without you having to type.

steps.title: Activating a voice assistant
steps.body: Say 'Hey Siri' or 'Okay Google', or press and hold the power button or home button (depending on your device). Then calmly speak your question or command.

steps.title: Asking or setting something
steps.body: Try, for example: 'What's the weather today?', 'Set a 10-minute timer', or 'Call [contact name]'.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Ask your phone's voice assistant out loud what time it is.

lessons.title: AI on your phone for everyday questions

steps.title: AI is more than just setting a timer
steps.body: Modern voice assistants (like Google's Gemini app) can also hold real AI conversations: explaining things, summarizing something, or thinking through a problem with you — just like ChatGPT, but on your phone.

steps.title: Having a text summarized or explained
steps.body: Got a long, complicated message (for example from the government)? Paste the text into the Gemini app and ask: 'Can you summarize this in simple language?'

steps.title: Getting help writing a message
steps.body: Need to write something tricky, like a complaint or a birthday message? Ask the AI for a draft, then adjust it in your own words afterward.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Open the Gemini app or Google Assistant on your phone and ask for a short explanation of a topic you're interested in.
